recent_posts.title: How To Use AI In Your Software with Semantic Kernel
recent_posts.summary: A video transcript walkthrough of Microsoft Semantic Kernel, explaining how developers can build LLM-powered applications beyond simple chatbots. Covers the framework's architecture including the kernel object, plugins, tool calling, and filters. Demonstrates a real-world RAG-based HR chatbot (EVA) built with ASP.NET Core, Azure OpenAI, SignalR for streaming, and PostgreSQL. Explains how tool/function calling works, how MCP fits into the picture, context window limitations, and multi-step reasoning. Also touches on using AI coding agents like GitHub Copilot to build such features, with a reminder that human code review remains essential.

recent_posts.title: How To Eat Safe With The "Eet Zeker" App
recent_posts.summary: .NET MAUI developer Judy discusses building "Eet Zeker" (Eat Safe), a mobile app for managing food allergies and intolerances. The app features a database of 20,000+ products, personalized allergen tracking, meal diary with symptom logging, and AI-powered alternative product recommendations using vector databases. Built with .NET MAUI using vertical slice architecture, the backend runs on Azure with MongoDB and Firebase authentication. Judy shares lessons learned about shipping products, avoiding perfectionism, and leveraging startup credits from Microsoft Founders Hub and other cloud providers.

recent_posts.title: Building a conference feedback platform with Azure and microservices
recent_posts.summary: Edward Kles demonstrates Spreaview, a conference feedback platform he built to help organizers collect and analyze speaker reviews. The system integrates with Sessionize for automatic conference data import, uses QR codes for easy attendee feedback submission, and provides speakers with a unified dashboard across multiple conferences. Built as a microservices architecture on Azure Container Apps with Dapr for service communication, the platform includes AI-powered topic matching, automated report generation, and a prize draw feature to incentivize feedback. The technical stack includes C#, .NET Aspire for orchestration, Cosmos DB for storage, Azure Service Bus for messaging, and GitHub Actions for CI/CD deployment.

recent_posts.title: Hot to use caching in .NET
recent_posts.summary: Comprehensive overview of caching options in .NET, covering in-memory cache, distributed cache with Redis, and the new hybrid cache introduced in .NET 9. Demonstrates practical implementation of each approach, discusses their trade-offs including stampede protection and distributed scenarios, and introduces Fusion Cache as a mature third-party alternative with advanced features like fail-safe mechanisms.

recent_posts.title: How to turbocharge you DevOps pipelines
How to use OpenAPI in .NET
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to implement and migrate to OpenAPI in .NET 9 using the new Microsoft-provided package, and explore its features, benefits, and integration with tools like scalar for better API documentation and client generation.

recent_posts.title: How to secure your NuGet supply chain flow
recent_posts.summary: Securing your NuGet supply chain is crucial for .NET developers who rely heavily on third-party packages. The post discusses the importance of knowing what packages are in your software and the risks associated with transitive dependencies. It introduces new features in .NET 9 for managing dependencies, including the dotnet list package command and the nuget audit mode. It also covers techniques to handle dependency confusion attacks, use of SBOM files for monitoring, handling sensitive licenses, and ensuring reproducible builds.

recent_posts.title: How to modernize legacy software using generative AI
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the modernization of legacy software using generative AI, specifically focusing on a case where XML-based code was converted to a modern development stack with TypeScript, Vue.js, and Node.js. It highlights the process and challenges encountered, including the iterative development cycle and the integration of human input to refine AI-generated outputs. The importance of prompt engineering and the role of Python as a bridge language in code transformations are also covered.

recent_posts.title: How to be more productive with Github Copilot Workspace
recent_posts.summary: The discussion highlights the capabilities of Github Copilot Workspace, an advanced AI tool designed to assist developers by generating code, explaining code structures, and automating repetitive tasks. The tool is currently in technical preview and aims to revolutionize coding workflows by enabling entire codebases to be written or modified using AI. Developers can interact with Copilot Workspace to create issues, generate code plans, and review AI-generated code, which helps accelerate development and improves productivity. The session also discussed how developers must still review AI suggestions to ensure code quality.

recent_posts.title: dotnetFlix - Learn all about the latest features in Azure Bicep
recent_posts.summary: The post features a discussion with Henry Bane about recent updates to Azure Bicep. The conversation covers advanced features and improvements introduced in the last 12 to 18 months, along with live demonstrations. Key highlights include custom types, user-defined functions, and deployment stacks. Henry also shares how locking stacks and handling resources through Azure Bicep can improve infrastructure management and deployment processes.
